host.period_status: Primary eclipse centers establish the recurrence. A second eclipse phase near 0.480 in the same fold supports the orbital period.
host.claim_basis: earlier public machine or TESS pipeline detection
host.prior_evidence: Earlier TESS-SPOC threshold-crossing event and Kostov et al. (2025) unvetted machine selection, Table 2. Fable 5.2 shortlisted the source. No earlier vetted same-clock eclipse identification was found in the sources searched.
host.interpretation: Both sharp eclipse phases recur across three TESS sectors. Difference images in two sectors favor this star for both phases. A separately resolved 6.4-arcsecond Gaia neighbour stays within 0.025 mag of baseline in five ZTF g and nine r exposures inside predicted eclipse windows, well below the approximately 40 percent fractional depth it would need in the TESS band. The target has three ZTF g primary-window exposures with a roughly 12 ppt median dip and 11 ppt baseline scatter.

unresolved_neighbour.note: The flux bound assumes Gaia Rp approximates a TESS flux ratio. Multiple ground-survey nights cover the expected windows in which the neighbour would need a very large eclipse.
